layouts.title: Full-bleed opening with deck title, subtitle, and organisation line.
layouts.section: Section divider with a large section number and title.
layouts.bullets: Title plus one to seven short statements.
layouts.two-column: Title plus two balanced statement groups for contrasts and objection handling.
layouts.metrics: Title plus two to four metric cards with label, value, and note.
layouts.quote: Oversized statement with attribution for message or voice-of-customer slides.
layouts.process: Title plus three to six ordered steps with numbers.
layouts.timeline: Title plus horizontal phase blocks with dates.
layouts.table: Title plus a readable table limited to six rows and four columns.
layouts.closing: Title plus decision statement, owner, and date.

roles.name: Title
roles.purpose: Name the promise of the session.
roles.guidance: One claim, the audience, and the date. No agenda text, no logos crowd.

roles.name: Agenda
roles.purpose: Set the route and the time budget.
roles.guidance: Use the section names that actually appear later; add minutes when the meeting is time-boxed.

roles.name: Section divider
roles.guidance: Number the section and restate the question it answers.

roles.name: Concept
roles.purpose: Explain one idea the audience must carry forward.
roles.guidance: Writing the title as a full sentence forces the slide to make a claim.

roles.name: Evidence
roles.purpose: Prove a claim with data, citation, or a demonstration.
roles.guidance: Every evidence slide carries at least one source entry; put the reading aid next to the data.

roles.name: Comparison
roles.guidance: Keep both columns at the same level of detail; state the recommendation in the title.

roles.name: Process
roles.purpose: Show an ordered method or workflow.
roles.guidance: Start each step with a verb; cap at six steps or group them.

roles.name: Timeline
roles.guidance: Dates or quarters only; no soft language such as soon.

roles.name: Data table
roles.purpose: Compare structured values the audience must read precisely.
roles.guidance: Six by four is the practical limit; move the rest to the appendix or a handout.

roles.name: Metrics
roles.purpose: Anchor the argument in two to four numbers.
roles.guidance: Every number needs a unit, a comparison, and a source line.

roles.name: Quote
roles.purpose: Let a customer, expert, or brief carry the message.
roles.guidance: Attribute with name, role, and permission status.

roles.name: Demonstration
roles.purpose: Show the product or process actually working.
roles.guidance: Have a recorded fallback; never depend on live network for the only copy of the proof.

roles.name: Decision
roles.guidance: Decision, owner, date, and the cost of not deciding.

roles.name: Summary
roles.purpose: Restate the argument and hand over the action.
roles.guidance: Mirror the opening promise; end with the action, not a thank-you.

roles.name: Appendix
roles.purpose: Hold backup detail that answers anticipated questions.
roles.guidance: Appendix slides are hidden by default and are not counted in pacing.
